title: NEET protest: Jantar Mantar walls wiped clean, but message stays on after Pradhan's exit
content: After the resignation of the education minister, Jantar Mantar came alive again with protesters on Sunday. Signs from earlier demonstrations lingered despite efforts to tidy up the area. First-time attendees joined long-term advocates, while both students and engaged citizens rallied in support. The scattered clusters highlighted their unwavering determination to continue fighting for their cause.

title: 'I am an average student': 19-yr-old ends life over low NEET marks in Maharashtra
content: Tragedy struck in Jalalpur village as a 19-year-old girl reportedly took her own life on Saturday. Authorities discovered a note revealing her distress over disappointing NEET re-examination results, where she scored 166, falling short of the 177 needed. This heartbreaking incident comes just weeks after another NEET-associated death in Nashik. Students are reminded to stay resilient and persevere through academic challenges.

title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, creates world record at just 15
content: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest Player of the Series winner. He achieved this milestone after India's T20I series victory over Zimbabwe. Sooryavanshi was the leading run-scorer with 151 runs across three innings. He scored a match-winning 81 runs in the final T20I match. This award followed a challenging series for the young cricketer in England.

title: US announces new visa restrictions to crack down on overseas fraud networks
content: The US government has introduced new visa restrictions targeting overseas criminal networks. These measures aim to combat cybercrime and extortion schemes that defraud American citizens. The policy builds upon President Donald Trump's executive order to prosecute cyber-enabled fraud. Chinese criminal organizations are specifically implicated in large-scale investment scams. Recent enforcement actions include sanctions and indictments against scam compound operators.

title: Anahat Singh: What's in the name? A word from Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation
content: The name Anahat comes from a line in Guru Nanak's Japji Sahib, discovered by her father on the day she was born. This is the story behind the name, the sporting family that shaped her, and the extraordinary journey that culminated in India's first-ever World Junior squash title at just 18.

title: Jeff Bezos ex-wife MacKenzie Scott helped write a 'donation playbook' for Snap founder
content: Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and Miranda Kerr have donated $550 million to erase medical debt. This significant contribution will benefit over 261,000 Californians facing financial hardship.  The donation follows a model pioneered by MacKenzie Scott, who has given billions to nonprofits.  The funds will be channeled through Undue Medical Debt, a prominent organization.  This initiative targets vulnerable residents, alleviating burdens of unpayable medical bills.

title: This AI data centre promised no Colorado River water. Now it wants 260mn gallons
content: Deemed as the largest AI data centre in the state, the 330-megawatt unit earlier promised to not use water from Colorado River. But now, the developer behind the project is suing for access to the river water which is already a threatened source of freshwater for 40 million people and the centre of countless disputes over water use in West.

title: A single tree can make 9 million seeds - and it's invading Queensland
content: An ornamental tree planted in Tahiti in 1937 now poses a serious biosecurity threat. This invasive miconia species aggressively invades forests and smothers native vegetation. A single mature tree can produce millions of seeds, rapidly spreading across landscapes. Queensland's World Heritage rainforests face irreversible ecological damage from this plant. Early detection and eradication efforts are crucial to protect these precious ecosystems.

title: Indian Idol 16 winner Jyotirmayee Nayak wins Rs 20L, wants to sing for Alia, Deepika
content: Jyotirmayee Nayak from Bhubaneswar has won the Indian Idol Season 16 trophy. She impressed judges and audiences with her powerful vocal performances throughout the competition. The talented singer received prize money of twenty lakh rupees after her victory. Nayak aspires to playback for Bollywood actresses Alia Bhatt and Deepika Padukone. She plans to focus on devotional music in her future musical endeavors.

title: DMK demands immediate NEET ban, seeks probe into Jantar Mantar violence
content: The DMK party is demanding an immediate nationwide ban on the NEET medical entrance examination. MP TR Baalu submitted an adjournment motion notice in the Lok Sabha seeking this ban. This demand follows a NEET UG paper leak and student protests across the nation. The DMK also called for an inquiry into the alleged use of weapons against students.

title: Chess legend Anand makes U-turn, rejoins FIDE election race
content: Viswanathan Anand has decided to contest the FIDE elections as Deputy President alongside presidential candidate Timur Turlov, reversing his earlier plan to step back for family reasons. The change follows Arkady Dvorkovich's exit from the race due to EU sanctions. Anand, currently FIDE's Interim President, said he wants to continue helping expand chess and backed Turlov's vision for the organisation.

title: 'Don't bother, I won't delete': Odisha BJP MP's daughter's post on Pradhan
content: A social media post by Aparajita Sarangi's daughter welcomed Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. This action caused discontent among Odisha BJP workers and leaders. Sarangi later publicly supported the senior BJP leader after his resignation. Her daughter refused to delete her controversial Instagram story. The contrasting stances generated widespread discussion across social media platforms.

title: From Jantar Mantar to Parliament: Govt, oppn brace for fight over NEET row, other issues
content: As the monsoon session reconvenes, tensions rise again over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal. Opposition factions are determined to maintain pressure on the administration following significant protests. Prime Minister Modi has introduced reforms for examinations and established a dedicated task force for student welfare. In response, Rahul Gandhi is targeting the government over police conduct. The government aims to introduce a bill designed to eradicate malpractice in examinations.

title: Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce's $2m gift moves families of fallen NYC heroes
content: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's generosity has brought heartfelt reactions from families of fallen New York City heroes who have long relied on Answer The Call for support. Widows and children shared emotional messages, with one saying, "I am in tears," while thanking the couple for their kindness. The donation is part of the couple's wider charitable efforts ahead of their wedding, but what touched these families most was the reassurance that the sacrifices of their loved ones will never be forgotten thanks to the couple's $2 million gift.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo to make Hollywood debut with Thierry Henry, Damian Lewis
content: Cristiano Ronaldo is entering a new arena beyond football with his first major television drama role in Day 1s, where he will serve as executive producer and appear on screen. The project, created through UR•Marv Studios with Matthew Vaughn, will also feature Thierry Henry and explore the behind-the-scenes world of British football through a fictional agent’s story.

title: CJP's win fuels call by 'E20 Janta Party' for no-ethanol option
content: A new E20 Janta Party has emerged, demanding consumer choice for 100% petrol. This group seeks the resignation of Nitin Gadkari, the transport minister. Transporters are supporting this campaign, planning a march to Parliament against E20 petrol. The party advocates for transparent fuel labelling and data publication. They are not seeking subsidies but consumer choice and clear information.

title: Why was Everson Griffen arrested? Gross misdemeanor charge explained
content: Former Minnesota Vikings star Everson Griffen was arrested in Minnesota after police alleged he violated the restrictions on his driver's license by operating a vehicle without the required ignition interlock device. The four-time Pro Bowler now faces a gross misdemeanor charge but insists the arrest had nothing to do with alcohol or drugs. Here's everything to know about why Griffen was taken into custody, what court documents reveal, his response on Instagram, the upcoming August 28 hearing, and how the latest legal issue impacts the former NFL defensive star.

title: 'Wapis nahi aane dega': Sooryavanshi's form triggers fresh debate over Samson's India return

With Samson dropped for the series and Abhishek Sharma struggling for runs, India’s opening combination remains a key selection debate ahead of the Asian Games.

title: Dhanush on National Awards row: 'Better films than Raayan existed'

The actor stated that some films simply fall into place on their own. He received a Special Mention for Captain Miller and Best Tamil Film for Raayan. Dhanush urged fans to celebrate his achievements as a Tamilian.

title: Oil prices fall 5%: Crude cools as US-Iran pause fuels hopes of diplomatic breakthrough
content: Oil prices dropped sharply as the United States and Iran held back from launching fresh strikes. This pause raised hopes that diplomacy could ease Middle East tensions and restore shipping. Brent crude futures fell significantly, trading at their lowest levels in nearly a week. Shipping through key trade routes remained subdued despite the pause in attacks. Uncertainty continues to linger over the conflict and its impact on energy markets.

title: 'I couldn't eat or drink for three days': Chanu's sacrifice behind CWG gold
content: The 31-year-old from Manipur lifted 85kg in the snatch and 105kg in the clean and jerk for a total of 190kg. She broke the Commonwealth and Commonwealth Games records in the snatch and also set new Commonwealth Games records in the clean and jerk and total lift.

The app has also climbed app store rankings significantly.

title: Student protest violence: Police may adopt 2022 formula to withdraw FIRs
content: Delhi Police may adopt a procedure used for past Red Fort violence cases.  This process involved police, Delhi government, and the lieutenant governor. Anti-social elements have been identified and booked in connection with the violence.

title: CWG 2026 medal table: Where India stands after Mirabai's golden hat-trick
content: India enjoyed a landmark Day 4 at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, winning three weightlifting medals including Mirabai Chanu’s historic third straight gold. Rishikanta Singh and Raja Muthupandi added silvers, while boxers Jadumani Singh and Preeti Pawar advanced with dominant wins. India also reached the swimming relay final, taking its overall medal tally to four.

title: India saw more than 5,000 child adoptions last year, highest in a decade
content: India saw a record 5,022 children adopted between April 2025 and March 2026. Domestic adoptions accounted for 4,603 children, while inter-country adoptions numbered 419. Special needs children adoption increased by twenty-five percent, reaching 392 last year. Adoptions of girls also rose by eight percent, continuing past trends. Relative and step-parent adoptions saw a significant fifty percent increase.

title: 'Jana Nayagan' BO day 4: Thalapathy Vijay and Pooja Hegde's film crosses Rs 100cr net
content: Thalapathy Vijay's 'Jana Nayagan' achieved impressive box office collections during its opening weekend. The film garnered over 32 crore net on its fourth day, showing a healthy increase. Its total India net collection has now surpassed 124 crore after four days. Worldwide gross collections for the movie have reached over 217 crore. The Tamil version registered strong occupancy, contributing significantly to its overall success.

title: PM Modi hails youth for taking India to arenas once beyond reach
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised young Indians for recent achievements.  PV Sindhu won the Japan Open badminton title, making the nation proud.  India's first privately developed orbital rocket, Vikram-1, also achieved a successful launch.  Students excelled in international science Olympiads, securing numerous medals.  These accomplishments demonstrate the nation's confident and capable young generation.

title: Berlin Pride attack suspect shot dead during police operation
content: The suspect involved in the deadly Pride attack on Saturday was shot and killed by Berlin police. This 21-year-old had a history of promoting Islamic State ideology online and had sought to join the group by going to Lebanon. His vehicle struck a crowd at the Christopher Street Day celebration, leading to one death and sixteen injuries.

title: 'Crimes against humanity' complaints filed against Bangladesh ex-president
content: Complaints were filed against former Bangladesh President Mohammed Shahabuddin on Sunday. These allegations concern crimes against humanity during the 2024 uprising against the government.  Shahabuddin resigned from his presidential post on Friday citing health complications.  The home minister stated the allegations do not warrant consideration by the tribunal.  However, the law minister confirmed Shahabuddin will face a corruption probe.

title: July FPI inflows touch Rs 42,000 crore, top February record

Total foreign inflows reached their strongest point this year, surpassing February's figures. Equity segment saw intense selling pressure earlier, with substantial outflows recorded. Debt markets remained resilient, attracting significant inflows throughout the year.
